# Football tactics reference

## Coordinates (never guess these)
- Pitch 105 × 68 m. **Absolute frame**: origin top-left, +x right, +y down; **home (H) always attacks +x**.
- `tactic_spec` positions use the **team-normalized frame**: each team is written as if it attacks +x, its own goal at
  x = 0, its **left** touchline at small y. The engine converts away players with a 180° rotation `(105 − x, 68 − y)`.
  So an away left-back at normalized (30, 10) is drawn at absolute (75, 58) — facing the home right wing. Correct.
- Landmarks (normalized, own goal at x = 0): penalty area x ≤ 16.5, y 13.84–54.16; halfway x = 52.5; opponent box
  x ≥ 88.5; goal mouth y 30.34–37.66; centre circle radius 9.15.
- Named zones (move targets): `.venv/Scripts/tms tactic zones` — e.g. `l_half_space_mid`, `r_wide_att`, `zone14`, `box`.
- Formation templates (roles by line, left → right): `.venv/Scripts/tms tactic templates`.

## Phases of play (`phase`) and who has the ball
| phase | team in possession | typical blocks (line_x = back line from own goal) |
|---|---|---|
| build_up | focus team | possession 20–28 m, opponent mid-block 28–34 m |
| progression | focus team | possession 32–40 m |
| final_third | focus team | possession 48–55 m, opponent low block 10–15 m |
| high_press | opponent (focus team presses) | pressing team 42–50 m; opponent builds from 10–15 m |
| mid_block | opponent | defending team 25–32 m, compact 24–28 m deep |
| low_block | opponent | defending team 10–15 m, 20–24 m deep |
| counter_press | opponent (just won it) | focus team 45–52 m, closing within 5 s |
| def_transition / att_transition | opponent / focus team | stretched shapes, 35–45 m deep |
`TS-13` enforces the holder; `tms tactic scaffold` applies these defaults.

## Realistic numbers (validators enforce many of them — see `config/rules.yaml`, `config/rules.d/`)
- Team vertical spread (outfield): compact 25–35 m, stretched ≤ 45 m. Lateral spread 30–60 m (block ≤ 45 m).
- Distance between lines 8–15 m; pressing distance to the ball carrier 1–3 m; marking distance 1–2.5 m.
- Teammates ≥ 4 m apart in a static shape; tokens are ~2 m wide, so opponents < 1.8 m look like a collision.
- Speeds: walk 1.5, jog 3.5, run 5.5, sprint 7.5 m/s (top speed ≤ 9.5). Ground pass 12–20 m/s, driven 18–25,
  lofted 12–18 horizontal, shot 20–32.
- Offside: an attacker beyond the second-last defender, in the opponent half, ahead of the ball, at the moment of a
  pass is offside. Demos must respect it unless the scene is *about* an offside trap.

## Vocabulary to use precisely
build-up shape (2-3, 3-2, 3-1), inverted full-back, false nine, half-spaces, overload / isolation, third-man run,
up-back-through, rest defence, counter-press (5-second rule), pressing trigger (back pass, poor touch, pass to a
full-back on the touchline, receiver facing his own goal), pressing trap, cover shadow, compactness, line height,
switch of play, overlap / underlap, rotations, pinning, width and depth, numerical / positional / qualitative superiority.

## Writing principles (tactic_spec.principles) — the heart of the video
- One idea each, **observable on a top-down pitch** within 3–8 seconds.
- `statement`: what happens and why it works, naming roles ("the right-back steps inside next to the 6, so two
  strikers cannot screen two pivots").
- `players`: the ids who demonstrate it. `visual_proof`: the exact moment the viewer must see.
- Count: 1 to max(2, min(5, ⌊target_s / 20⌋)) (`TS-12`). Fewer, sharper principles beat many vague ones.
- Every weakness should have a counter (`counters[].targets`), and triggers name both the cue and the response.

## Common mistakes reviewers reject
- Shapes that would never happen (back line at halfway in a low block, GK at 30 m, wingers in the centre without
  a reason). Justify unusual positions with a `note` or by naming the player in a principle (`TS-07`).
- Mirroring instead of rotating the away team (left/right swapped).
- Principles that are slogans ("dominate the midfield") rather than mechanisms.
